messages:
olivia: Brought up s3-embed-v2 int8 on staging, per-channel quantization. ran full eval-suite (webqa, msrv1, internal-retrieval). sharing quick sanity numbers and plots.
sam: Nice — can you paste the recall@k? especially @10 and @1 for webqa.
ravi: also share cosine distribution / mean/variance, we saw weird compression last time with int8.
olivia: WebQA recall@1: 0.56 (fp16 baseline 0.62)
olivia: WebQA recall@10: 0.84 (fp16 baseline 0.87)
olivia: MSRv1 recall@1: 0.48 -> 0.53 (slightly better on this set, weird)
olivia: Cosine mean across positive pairs (fp16): 0.31, (int8): 0.22
olivia: Cosine stddev (fp16): 0.14, (int8): 0.12
maria: so overall drop on webqa but not msrv1 — likely dataset sensitivity to quant noise / distribution shift.
ravI: @olivia can you confirm vectors were L2-normalized after quantization? that matters for cosine.
olivia: yes we ran normalize_post_quant = True in the pipeline.
sam: did you try rescaling the int8 outputs? e.g. apply learned multiplier per-dataset or per-layer?
olivia: ran quick per-dataset temperature cal: multiplying embeddings by 1.08 recovers recall@1 to 0.59 on webqa, recall@10 to 0.86.
ravI: interesting. can you push the distribution plots? I want to see cluster separation (silhouette).

olivia: attaching quick summary (pasted):
```
Dataset    recall@1 (fp16->int8)    recall@10 (fp16->int8)    sil_score_fp16    sil_score_int8
webqa      0.62 -> 0.56             0.87 -> 0.84              0.42              0.35
msrv1      0.51 -> 0.53             0.79 -> 0.80              0.31              0.33
```

olivia: UMAP plots: clusters more compressed in int8, nearest-neighbor distances shrink ~10-12% on average.
eval-bot: eval run 1867201234 completed: webqa, msrv1, internal-retrieval. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/1867201234/ (models, plots, raw-metrics)
maria: thanks — I think next steps: 1) try per-dataset scaling factor (learned on small holdout), 2) test per-dim bias correction (mean-shift), 3) run int8 w/ fp16 KV-cache hybrid if possible.
ravI: also try re-quantizing with symmetric vs asymmetric quant; last time asymmetric preserved cosine better.
sam: CPU-side indexing (FAISS) — did you reindex int8 vectors? compression in vector store can interact.
olivia: reindexed the faiss flat index with int8 vectors; will run a separate comparison with storing fp16 index but serving int8 to compute distances.
maria: for rollout plan: don't ship int8 to prod for webqa until we can get recall within 0.01 of fp16 or put fallback to fp16 for critical routes.
ravI: Agreed. Also add a differential eval on a small user-sim dataset (query logs holdout) — that's usually most sensitive.
sam: can we automate the per-dataset calibration? e.g. run a 1k-pair holdout and compute multiplier + shift automatically in the onboarding job.
olivia: yes I can add a calibration step to the onboarding script. quick pseudocode I used manually:
```
# calibration
E_fp = load_embeddings(fp16_holdout)
E_q = load_embeddings(int8_holdout)
alpha = argmax_alpha recall(E_fp, alpha * E_q)
apply scale = alpha
```

maria: perfect. other ask: add a unit test for cosine distribution shift (mean diff < 0.05) to catch regressions in CI.
ravI: +1 on test. also record silhouette and recall@10 in the model metadata onboard artifact.

olivia: I'll push changes to the onboarding pipeline today and run another sweep with symmetric quant and per-dataset scaling. will post results in this thread.
sam: thanks, @olivia :thumbsup:
maria: tagging for visibility: @team-eng-ml
olivia: side note: msrv1 improvement may be due to different length distributions — int8 seems to help short docs? need to probe.

olivia: follow-up last_message: scheduled larger sweep for tomorrow 06:00 UTC, will include fp16 baseline, int8 symmetric, int8 asymmetric, and int8 + scaling. artifacts will include per-query recall and UMAP images.
